chapter: Moten band, arranging and the guitar
title: The 1929 band and which Moten numbers he arranged
summary: They check the 1929 personnel and the 1932 session, and Durham lists the titles he arranged, such as New Vine Street Blues and Mary Lee.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Well, now, let me just check this thing out. Yeah, you come into this band, according to this book, in 1929.
With -- I didn't realize that, Walter Page had been with Basie before. So 1929, --
Yeah. Page -- you've got Page, Willie Washington, drums, Basie, Leroy Barrie, guitar, Jack Weston and Eddie Baer, Ben Webster, Eddie Durham, Lips Page (inaudible).
Yeah, '29. I got a picture out there, on an album. I got a picture out there, Lips Page, Lips Page, Count Basie, myself, Dan Miner and Bing Page and Susan.
Well, now, this band, though, -- see, now, everybody talks about the records of 1932, with Morton Swing, Toby, New Orleans, Lafayette, --
Yeah, do you have that record?
Yeah, I've got it. But the thing --

I mean, this is the same band that -- well, Buster Smith has taken Washington's place and Harlan Leonard is added for these records. But the band in 1929, you know, where they're doing -- I don't know whether you did any of those arrangements, see, right down there.

(Inaudible.) I did the Mary Lee, and Bootleg, I forgot now. Let's see, New Vine Street Blues I did, Bandbox. I didn't do the (inaudible), I don't think. Small Black I didn't do. (Inaudible) Blues, I might have did that. Yeah, I think so. Wished I Could Be Blue, I think I did that with Rushing. That To Do I did, Get Going I didn't do. I don't remember Lisa Lee. Would You Be My Baby, I think I did that. And the New Morton Swing, the Count -- I named Basie the Count, so that's when they started to call him Count, from then on.
